summary: New Moon Airport (NMP) is a small regional airfield serving the rural community of Basalt in northern Queensland, Australia. It primarily supports general aviation, private aircraft, and occasional charter flights rather than scheduled commercial service. The airport features a single unsealed runway typical of remote Australian outback airfields, providing access to an otherwise road-isolated region.
faqs:
Q: Does New Moon Airport offer commercial passenger flights?
A: No, New Moon Airport is a small general aviation airfield with no scheduled commercial airline service. It is primarily used by private pilots, charter operators, and aerial work aircraft.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport has basic infrastructure including a runway and possibly minimal pilot facilities, but it does not offer passenger terminals, baggage services, or on-site fuel guaranteed at all times. Visitors should arrange their own provisions.

Q: Can I fly into Basalt on a private aircraft?
A: Yes, private and charter aircraft can use New Moon Airport, though pilots should check current conditions and runway suitability before arrival as this is a small, remote strip.

Q: Is the airport open 24 hours?
A: As an uncontrolled airfield, New Moon Airport can technically be used at any time, but operations are typically limited to daylight hours for safety reasons.
transport_tips: Getting to and from New Moon Airport typically requires a private vehicle, as there is no public transport serving this remote airfield. Visitors should arrange rental car pickup or coordinate with a local contact for ground transportation in advance. The drive from nearby towns in the region requires preparation, as roads may be unsealed and distances considerable.
local_tip: Carry extra fuel and water when flying into New Moon, as the surrounding Basalt region has limited services and the nearest town with full amenities is a significant drive away.
